cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: Schema design is deciding tables, columns, data types, keys, constraints and indexes. A schema migration is a versioned, repeatable script that changes the schema. Design from access patterns, the hot reads and writes, not from entities that feel natural.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: Normalize by default; denormalize only for measured read-heavy paths. Keep migrations backward compatible with expand and contract: add the new structure, backfill in batches off the request path, switch the code, then drop the old structure in a later release.

questions.q: Why not rename a column in one migration?
questions.a: During a rolling deploy old instances still query the old name and fail. Use expand and contract instead.

questions.q: What are the expand and contract steps?
questions.a: Expand (add new), backfill in batches, switch code over, then contract (drop old) later.
For read-heavy, latency-sensitive paths where a join is too costly, accepting duplicated data you must keep in sync.
